previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a 58-year-old male with acute myeloid leukemia in remission following double cord blood transplant, was admitted with fevers, rigors, and hypoxic respiratory failure. He was found to have Stenotrophomonas maltophilia bacteremia, likely from his central venous catheter, and was treated with IV antibiotics after line removal. His oxygen requirements improved, and repeat cultures were negative. He developed acute kidney injury, attributed to a benign lab effect from Bactrim, which resolved after discontinuation. An echocardiogram revealed a reduced ejection fraction of 40%, and he was discharged on heart failure medications. An infected ingrown toenail was surgically treated, and he completed a course of oral antibiotics. Mental status changes were evaluated with a normal brain MRI. He was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up planned for cardiology, nephrology, pulmonary, podiatry, and ophthalmology.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ year old male day diffuse joint pain and painful toes; 
recently hospitalized with hypoxic repiratory failure and found 
to have stentotrophomonas bacteremia.
.  
1. Toe pain - Presented with history of chronic in-grown toe 
nails. s/p toe nail biopsy at previous hospitalization. Wound 
culture with coag positive Staph aureus. At previous 
hospitalization, was initially treated with vancomycin (2 
doses), then given at discharge 5 day course of Augmentin. On 
admission for present hospitalization, vancomycin IV was 
started. Podiatry was also consulted; excisional debridement of 
left first toe was performed. Pain and erythema improved 
considerably on IV antibiotics. On discharge, patient was 
provided information to arrange follow-up with podiatry in one 
week. A PICC line was also placed to allow the patient to 
complete additional 7 day course of vancomycin IV.
.  
2. Stenotrophomonas bactermia - Patient did not complete 
antibiotic course for Stenotrophomonas bacteremia at last 
infection secondary to renal failure and hyperkalemia which was 
thought to be due to Bactrim. Received 12 of 14 day course. 
Stenotrophomonas sensitivities from previous hospitalization 
show sensitivity to Bactrim and ceftazidime. On admission, 
patient was restarted on ceftazidime based on the possibility 
that his diffuse arthralgias may be due to a systemic infection. 
Blood cultures were no growth to date. Ultrasound at former 
___ site was ultrasounded to assess for abscess - no 
abscess or clot was seen. Given patient's improvement on 
steroids (as explained below), ceftazidime was stopped prior to 
discharge.
.  
3. Diffuse arthralgias/myalgias - Has history of aspergillosis, 
which can in itself cause severe muscle aches. Has been on 
voriconazole. Differential diagnosis on presentation also 
included GVH, avascular necrosis given longterm steroid use, 
rhemautoid arthritis, osteoarthritis, gout, Still's, Lyme. No 
outdoor exposure. Voriconazole was continued at home regimen of 
300mg ___ Q12. Hip films were negative for avascular necrosis. 
Neurology was consulted given that patient's outpatient workup 
for these issues included an EMG - their recommendation was to 
hold off on the EMG as would likely not alter management. Two to 
three days after presentation, patient was tried on increased 
dose of prednisone. Within ___ hours, patient's pain 
completely resolved. On discharge, patient was on prednisone 
20mg ___ QAM and 15mg ___ QPM. Further dose adjustment/tapering is 
to be done on an outpatient basis. Overall, the aches were 
thought to be secondary to GVH.
.  
4. Renal failure - Creatinine better than at discharge, although 
considerably higher than ___ of this year. Source unclear, 
although during previous admission creatinine rose steadily on 
IV bactrim, furosemide, lisinopril. Creatinine continued to 
improve during this hospitalization with IV fliuds, increased ___ 
intake.
.  
5. Acute myelogyenous leukemia - s/p allo SCT. Continued 
Cellcept per home regimen. Monitored ___ blood counts. 
Transfused for platelets <10. Transfused for hematocrit <25.  
.  
6. Hyperkalemia - On presentation. Unclear reason. At last 
admission was thought to be related to renal failure, which was 
thought to be secondary to Bactrim. Hyperkalemia improved on 
admission with Kayexelate. Patient was given calcium and 
furosemide given EKG changes associated with hyperkalemia. 
Resolved without further intervention. Potassium levels were 
checked twice ___.
.
7. History of aspergillosis - Continued voriconazole 300 ___ Q12H 
per home regimen.  
.  
8. Hypertension - During previous admission was restarted on 
carvedilol; ACE inhibitor was held secondary to elevated 
creatinine.  Continued to hold ACE inhibitor as creatinine 
improved.   
.  
9. Neuropathy - Continued neurontin per home regimen.
.  
10. Diabetes mellitus - Continued glargine 4U at bedtime. 
Sliding scale insulin with QID blood glucose checks. Of note, 
blood glucose ran high after BID steroids were started.

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  ___ male with bilateral hip pain, history of long-term
steroid use.  Assess for avascular necrosis.

FINDINGS:  Single AP view of the pelvis and two views of the hips,
bilaterally, without prior comparison.  There is no evidence for fracture or
dislocation.  The hips appear normal bilaterally without evidence for
significant degenerative change.  There is no sclerosis, subchondral lucency,
or deformity of the femoral heads to suggest avascular necrosis.  The
sacroiliac joints and pubic symphysis are normal.  There are no suspicious
lytic or sclerotic osseous lesions.  Mild degenerative changes in the lumbar
spine.

IMPRESSION:  Mild degenerative changes in the lumbar spine.  No fracture,
dislocation, or evidence of avascular necrosis.

HISTORY:  Left arm swelling.

LEFT UPPER EXTREMITY ULTRASOUND.

Comparison is made to ___ exam.

Grayscale and Doppler sonograms of the left internal jugular, subclavian,
axillary, brachial, basilic, and cephalic veins demonstrate normal flow,
compressibility, augmentation, and waveforms.  No intraluminal thrombus is
identified.

IMPRESSION:

No evidence of left upper extremity DVT.

HISTORY:  Status post removal of tunneled central venous catheter for
infection in patient with AML and persistent tenderness at tunnel site.
Evaluate for focal collection.

Comparison is made to ___ and ___ chest CTs.

LIMITED CHEST WALL ULTRASOUND.

At the patient's site of previous catheter superficially within the
subcutaneous tissues of the left chest is an irregular heterogeneous
collection with minimal increased through transmission measuring approximately
1.9 x 3.9 x 1.5 cm, which appears to extend towards the subclavian vein in a
more linear tubular fashion.  No significant peripheral hyperemia or internal
vascularity is appreciated.  The appearance of the collection is likely not
significantly changed in size from most recent chest CT where the largest
component measured approximately 2.2 x 2.4 cm and displayed a similar smaller
linear collection extending towards the subclavian vein along the site of
previous catheter.

IMPRESSION:

Heterogeneous collection, not significantly changed from most recent chest CT
at site of prior ___ catheter.  Based on density on prior CT, this likely
represents a hematoma, although superinfection/abscesses is not completely
excluded.  Based on clinical symptoms, this could be aspirated under
ultrasound- guidance if needed.

BILATERAL TOES, ___.

HISTORY:  ___ man with AML, status post core blood transplant, now
with pus draining from the first digits, bilaterally, growing MRSA; evaluate
for evidence of osteomyelitis.

FINDINGS:  Three non-standing views of each foot compared with the recent
study of the right foot, dated ___ (there is no previous imaging of the
left foot); no further localizing information or radiographic skin marker is
provided.  The overall appearance of the right foot is unchanged.
Specifically, no discrete first digital soft tissue defect to suggest frank
ulcer and no retained radiopaque foreign body is identified.  There is no
definite periosteal reaction, cortical discontinuity or medullary lucency to
specifically suggest osteomyelitis.

Views of the left foot are similarly unremarkable.  Though gauze material
overlies the left first digit, no underlying soft tissue defect to suggest
discrete ulcer or retained radiopaque material is seen.  There is no
periosteal reaction, cortical discontinuity or medullary lucency to
specifically suggest osteomyelitis.

IMPRESSION:  No change in the appearance of the right foot or specifically,
the right first digit since the radiographs dated ___, and no specific
radiographic evidence of osteomyelitis in either first digital ray.

COMMENT:  Persistent clinical concern would be best addressed by dedicated
targeted enhanced MR examination.

STUDY:  PICC line placement.

INDICATION:  IV access needed for AML drug delivery.

Procedure was explained to the patient.  A timeout was performed with two
patient identifiers.

RADIOLOGISTS:  Dr. ___ the procedure.  Dr ___ attending
radiologist supervised the procedure.

TECHNIQUE:  Using sterile technique and local anesthesia, the right basilic
vein was punctured under direct ultrasound guidance using a micropuncture set.
Hard copies of ultrasound images were obtained before and immediately after
establishing intravenous access.  A peel-away sheath was then placed over a
guidewire and a double-lumen PICC line measuring 35 cm in length was then
placed through the peel-away sheath with its tip positioned in the SVC under
fluoroscopic guidance.  Position of the catheter was confirmed by a
fluoroscopic spot film of the chest.

The peel-away sheath and guidewire were then removed.  The catheter was
secured to the skin, flushed, and a sterile dressing applied.

The patient tolerated the procedure well.  There were no immediate post-
procedural complications.

IMPRESSION:  Uncomplicated ultrasound and fluoroscopically guided double-lumen
PICC line placement via the right basilic venous approach.  Final internal
length is 35 cm, with the tip positioned in the SVC.  The line is ready to
use.
